title: An interview study about the experiences of older patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain and pain education
summary:
Persistent pain in muscles, joints or bones can be very distressing. It can make everyday life difficult, for example when walking, climbing stairs, shopping or taking part in leisure activities. Such pain often leads to limitations, particularly in older people.
An important part of pain management is providing people with good information about pain. This is known as pain education. It involves, for example, explaining why pain occurs, why it can persist and what can help in daily life. Such information can help people manage their pain more effectively.
However, little is currently known about how this information should best be presented to older people. It should be easy to understand, helpful and appropriate to the life situation of older people.
That is why this study is interviewing people aged 60 and over. People who have had pain in their muscles, joints or bones for a long time and have previously received information about pain as part of their treatment are eligible to take part.
In a one-to-one interview, participants can describe how they found this information. The aim of the study is to gain a better understanding of what older people with chronic pain need when they receive information about pain. The results will help to make such information more understandable, helpful and better suited to older people in the future.
conditions: Chronic pain disorder involving both physical and psychological factors

interventions.name: Semi-structured, guided interviews with a narrative component will be conducted with older patients (aged 60 and older) who have chronic musculoskeletal pain and who have received pain education as part of their pain management treatment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain (lasting ≥ 3 months)

Patients receiving at least one form of pain education as a therapeutic intervention (e.g. as part of a stay at a pain clinic or as part of outpatient treatment)
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under the age of 60
Patients who have received pain education in connection with non-musculoskeletal conditions (e.g. migraine, irritable bowel syndrome, CRPS)
Patients with cognitive impairments that prevent them from giving informed consent or participating in an interview
Patients whose German language skills are insufficient to conduct the interview
Patients experiencing an acute episode of pain or an acute medical crisis
Patients with severe mental health conditions currently requiring treatment
